title: Percentages — Foundations

steps.title: Percent means per hundred
steps.content: A percent is a ratio with denominator 100. 25% means 25 out of every 100. In placement papers, convert fluently between percent, fraction and decimal before solving the story.
steps.tip: Write the percent as a fraction over 100 first; simplify only after that.

steps.title: Finding the whole from a part
steps.content: If a percent of a number equals a known value, divide by the percent (as a fraction) to recover the whole. Example: 20% of N = 50 → N = 50 × 100/20 = 250.
steps.formula: If p% of N = A, then N = A × 100 / p
steps.tip: Always ask: is the given amount the part or the whole?

steps.title: Recover the base
steps.prompt: 30% of a number is 90. What is the number?
hints: The 90 is the part, not the whole.

steps.title: Percentage change
steps.content: Percentage increase = (new − old) / old × 100. Percentage decrease uses the same form with a negative change. The base is always the original value unless the question says otherwise.

steps.title: Compute the increase
steps.prompt: A salary rises from ₹20,000 to ₹23,000. What is the percentage increase?
hints: Subtract to get the absolute increase first.

steps.title: Wrong base error
steps.prompt: A value falls from 80 to 60. A student computes 20/60 × 100 ≈ 33%. What went wrong?
options: The base must be the original value 80, so decrease is 25%
You must always use 100 as the base
steps.explanation: Percentage change uses the starting value: 20/80 × 100 = 25%.
hints: Put the original in the denominator.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Percentage change uses the new value as the base.
common_misconceptions.correction: Always divide by the original value unless the question specifies otherwise.

common_misconceptions.misconception: x% of y is the same as y% of x only sometimes.
common_misconceptions.correction: x% of y always equals y% of x because both equal xy/100.
